take_homes: Don't split into several agents by default. Split only where the access, the dialect or the stance differs. The access test matters most for employee data.
Handoffs between agents are where things go quietly missing, and a review of how they worked together doesn't tell me the answer is true.
An agent can propose and wait for approval instead of acting. That is the kind of question I can take to my leadership team.

monday.move: Ask my DPO and the works council representative what would be allowed before I put any employee data near an agent. Then try the crux exercise on my own people-strategy question, using no personal data.
monday.stop_condition: If the DPO or works council says no or not yet, I stop at documents without personal data.
monday.blocker: Employee data in an AI tool needs the works council and the DPO, and I haven't asked them yet.

misconception.why: The module was about how to build and split agents and never about roles or headcount. The access example touched people only through data. I still expect the first question from my leadership team to be which roles go.

one_line: Good on when not to use several agents and on the risk at handoffs, but I got no picture of what it means for people and roles. I spent half an hour managing windows.
